text:
Gem Black Market · 9 participants · 3 rounds

1. Cards and the Lead Player Auction
Use 13 cards: diamond 5 and 6, gold 4 and 5, silver 2, 3, and 4, copper 1, 1, 2, and 2, and bombs -6 and -4. In a continuous 10-player run, add one copper 1 card for 14 cards. Draw the default order, and the highest bidder in a private Piece auction becomes the lead player for round 1. Only the winning bidder pays Pieces. Tied bidders raise their total bids for a reauction; if they do not raise further, they agree on the lead player. If no agreement is reached, follow the default order. Starting with the lead player and following the default order, deal one card face down to each person, each of the three buyer slots, and the trash. Initially, you check your own card; afterward, you may check your own card only on your turn.

2. Exchanges and Information
Every round, you must exchange cards once in forward order and once in reverse order. The lead player acts first and last. Swap with another participant, one buyer slot, or the trash. Anyone holding a bomb may exchange only with another participant. If someone else takes my bomb, I immediately receive 3 points; if I hand it over myself, there is no bonus. Once during the entire game, you may pay one Piece to privately inspect one buyer slot or the trash. The 3-minute exchange time limit is implemented by giving everyone sequential opportunities to talk for up to 4 cycles. Paid inspection may also be chosen during conversation, and the exchanging player receives a separate opportunity for paid inspection on their own turn. Public statements, whispers in the same location, and discussion room conversations are available, and promises do not bind exchanges.

3. Round Scoring
After two exchanges, reveal all cards. Earn Victory Points by multiplying your card's number by the number of buyer cards of the same type as your gem. If you score with a diamond, you also receive one Piece. A bomb deducts the negative value printed on it. Reveal cumulative Victory Points. The holder of the -6 bomb becomes the next lead player; if there is none, the holder of the -4 bomb does; if neither exists, the current lead player remains.

4. Manito and Final Results
Manito relationships form a randomly drawn one-directional ring. I privately learn only the person whose score I affect. The person who affects my score is revealed at the end. After 3 rounds, multiply my cumulative Victory Points by the cumulative Victory Points of the Manito who affects me to determine my final Victory Points. Break ties using the simulator's default order. The top 3 go to Living Quarters, the single last-place player is eliminated, and the rest go to Prison Wing. The 1st-place player uses Alliance Token to move one person from Prison Wing to Living Quarters. Receive 1 Piece for final Victory Points of at least 1, or a total of 2 for at least 10.

5. Negotiation and Strategy Notes
After reviewing the game rules and before Manitos are revealed, everyone negotiates and talks for 12 cycles. On each exchange turn, everyone may also talk for up to 4 cycles to exchange proposals and responses. In each cycle, everyone selects one conversation action, and the exchanging player speaks first. After deciding whether to pay for card inspection, the exchanging player writes one private strategy note based on their own card and the conversation heard so far, then decides whom or what to exchange with. Only that player can view this note.

6. Tied Auction Negotiation
If multiple players submit the same highest bid, everyone talks for up to 5 cycles before the reauction or final agreement. The tied candidates and highest bid are revealed, and players may discuss rebidding and nominating the lead player. Only tied participants rebid and vote on the final nomination. Pre-exchange conversation and tied-bid negotiation end early if everyone passes in a cycle. Pre-game negotiation runs for 12 cycles.

7. Pre-game Sequence
After pre-game conversation ends, Manito notification and the Piece auction occur in the same stage. Everyone privately receives their own Manito and simultaneously submits a private bid with no intervening conversation. After the auction, everyone receives up to 5 additional cycles of conversation. This conversation also ends early if everyone passes in a cycle. Then deal the cards and begin round 1.

8. Relationship Assessment Updates
Review affinity and trust ratings at the end of each negotiation segment, when the lead player auction results are revealed, and after paid card inspection and exchange are completed. Also review them after card-reveal scoring, final Manito and score disclosure, and Alliance Token use. Participants assess based on new conversations and actions visible to them and compare promises with actual results using recent observations. Update when there is new evidence; only the participant can see the scores and reasons.

9. Private Pre-game Strategy Preparation
After the game rules are revealed and before the first conversation, each person privately completes 3 stages: drafting, reviewing risks and alternatives, and finalizing a negotiation plan. At each stage, carry forward and revise your previous strategy summary, leaving the result as a short strategy summary visible only to you. Refer to the final summary in subsequent negotiations as well. At this point, Manitos and cards have not yet been revealed, and you cannot view anyone else's preparation.

10. Shortening Pre-exchange Conversation and Ending Early
Each pre-exchange conversation allows up to 4 turns per participant. The exchanging player acts first on each conversation turn and may choose to end the conversation and proceed with the exchange from the first opportunity. In that case, skip the remaining people's statements and conversation turns. Only the exchanging player may end conversation early. After it ends, they decide whether to pay for inspection, organize their private strategy, and then exchange. Pre-game conversation remains 12 turns, and post-auction conversation and tied-bid negotiation remain up to 5 turns.
